directEvidence.finding: Catalogue PG14 through PG18 columns all list pg_hashids 1.2.1. No package revision or binary hash is supplied in this row.

Source stage downloads upstream v1.2.1 archive, checks SHA256 74576b992d9277c92196dd8d816baa2cc2d8046fe102f3dcd7f3c3febed6822a, extracts it, then build stage runs PGXS make/install. Only named pg_hashids change appends trusted = true to the control file; no source patch appears in either stage.

Complete recursive public tree (truncated=false) contains no path with hashids and no pg_hashids patch. Dockerfile itself contains hashids stages. Other extensions have explicit COPY compute/patches/... and patch commands.

Public cloud extension test matrix lists PG16 and PG17 only. Public compute tree has postgres-v14 through postgres-v17 submodules and no postgres-v18. Recipe most recent path commit observed is 84a2556c9ff194cf789c93cafc65167132e76409 dated 2025-07-23. Cannot identify this public recipe as the deployed PG18 image.

Both scalar and array encoders allocate bytes_encoded while the text header and copy require bytes_encoded + VARHDRSZ. Allocation rounding is not a safety contract; no input-only admission repairs this native invariant over the full requested domain.

For min_hash_length>0, first effective guard sets str=p+1; lottery=*str++ then while((ch=*str)) reads past the terminator when guard is final. Effective guards depend on salt/alphabet. SQL exposes the four native symbols, not initialized guard state.

Commit 4bda0a7b7e7abbbf6e47ff26099771f52c891f6c (2019-09-06) adds VARHDRSZ to scalar allocation only. Its array allocation still lacks VARHDRSZ. This commit is later than tag 16907249ccbc300b31c89c3eccd6042c5674505f (2018-01-12).
Commit f692cf6b54cd4afd01f4dc2c0c2241c5e609f561 (2020-05-11) converts both encoder results to cstring_to_text_with_len; current upstream retains this conversion.

At upstream head 8c404dd86408f3a987a3ff6825ac7e42bd618b98 the trailing-guard skip/lottery/read pattern remains; bounded output count does not bound this input read. Static defect evidence, not a new crash probe.

Current source control default_version=1.3; upgrade SQL makes all twenty functions IMMUTABLE STRICT and switches shared-library references to MODULE_PATHNAME. Selected 1.2.1 SQL is non-STRICT and defaults to VOLATILE; current manifest captures strict=false, volatility=volatile, parallel=unsafe. Latest published tag is v1.2.1 and releases API is empty at observation; master containing 1.3 is not a newly tagged fix release.

Extension archives can be downloaded from deployment-provided remote_ext_base_url plus ext_path. Public code does not reveal a deployed PG18 pg_hashids archive/build digest. No artifact retrieved, no nm/objdump, no provider API/database calls. Symbol presence alone would prove neither allocation size nor input bounds.

remediation.requiredAuthority: Parent must obtain Neon-authoritative PG18 package recipe/patch set and deployment-to-artifact linkage, or authorize a provider-maintainer native patch/backport. Child has no authority to install or replace provider libraries, change selected version/manifest, or promote acceptance.

quantifiedMinimum.limit: Necessary native fixes and member counts, not an exhaustive estimate of patch work or a safety certification.

minimumNativeWork: Repair both scalar and array text result allocation with correct VARHDRSZ size or PostgreSQL text conversion, preserving selected output bytes and SQL signatures.

Repair bounds in native decode after guard skip and before lottery/parse reads for the full admitted string domain; characterize malformed-input outcome instead of substituting a JS algorithm or blanket-rejecting padding.

Audit selected wrapper/library for malloc lifetime (free after PG_RETURN is unreachable), null/array shape, initialization errors, byte ABI and overflow. These remain pending native acceptance concerns; the two named fixes are necessary, not an exhaustive safety proof.
remediation.identityDecision: A provider-maintained backport retaining extversion=1.2.1 needs authoritative patch revision and binary SHA256 tied to PG18/architecture/build. Parent must decide whether the existing provider profile permits this patch revision and recapture any changed SQL/codec semantics. Replacing with 1.3 requires selected-version/manifest and semantic review and still does not fix the observed decoder input-bound pattern.
